recheck.why:
Almost everything checks out — lint is 1.000 clean, the pack-consistency checker returns zero findings for this slug, the retrieval budget balances to the call, all eight slots are spent, role/level are correct, and the cross-references to siblings are reciprocal and accurate. But the Human verification section contradicts step 5 on the skill's central deliverable (the coverage-directory verdict), and following it literally produces the exact collision step 5 warns against. That is a wrong answer produced by the checklist meant to catch wrong answers, so it blocks.

(1) DV correctness: sound apart from one gotcha nuance (see remaining). The scheduler/farm material is right: wall-clock kill vs OOM kill told apart by last-line completeness, node-local scratch copy-back, inherited-environment absence, retry masking intermittents, union-not-sum merge semantics, cross-elaboration bin mismatch, and the seed argument ("a directed test at forty seeds is forty identical runs at forty times the cost") are all correct and well-argued.
(2) Budget: exact. Declared 4 Globs / 12 Greps (4 membership + 1 sentinel + 6 flow-file + 1 closure plan) / 9 windowed Reads (4 list heads + 4 flow-file windows + 1 closure plan). Step 1 spends the Globs, step 2 the 4+4, step 3 explicitly reuses step 2's windows ("Work from the windows step 2 opened"), step 4 spends the sentinel Grep plus closure plan Grep+Read, step 5 spends 2 of the 6 flow-file Greps, step 6 the remaining 4 plus the windows. Nothing overruns; the whole-file Read under ~300 lines is declared as an alternative to the windows. Step 6's handoff compares paths the engineer supplies, spending nothing.
(3) Nothing proprietary is asserted: no simulator, scheduler, coverage tool, flag or message string appears anywhere in the file (grep for vcs|verdi|urg|imc|xcelium|questa|lsf|bsub|slurm|ucdb|covdb returns nothing). Every such fact is a slot.
(4) Every slot is spent, and the four profile facts are spent at named steps. The "narrower than the profile" paragraph is honest and correct: Coverage directory expression vs Coverage output, and Regression lists vs Regression summary, are genuinely different facts, and the dv-repo-orientation "Test list" cross-reference is real (that slot exists at line 44 of that skill).
(5) Handoff block: every field has a step, and every enum token is assignable (checker C005 clean). seeds/cov mode/pass rule are declared local, which matches handoff-vocabulary's local-by-default rule; `cov mode` correctly qualifies the reserved held noun `mode`; `coverage`, `findings`, `tests`, `tier`, `budget` are free text here and free text or a different sense elsewhere, which the registry explicitly permits ("a name used as an enum in one skill and as free text in another cannot mismatch").
(6) role dv-infra-engineer / level senior — exact. review-by 2027-06-14 is unique in the pack and ~10 months out.
(7) `python -m semiskill.cli lint skills/dv-regression-tiering-farm` → "[approve 1.000] clean; 1/1 clean, 0 errors, 0 advisories, 1 predicted to publish".
(8) No — I would not hand it over until the step 5 / verification contradiction is repaired. It is one sentence, but it is the sentence a reader applies last.
remaining: BLOCKER — the Human verification checklist contradicts step 5 on the coverage-directory expression, and obeying it produces the defect step 5 names. Line 249: "the coverage directory expression has exactly one component that varies per run, every component is labelled scope, run or noise, the build tag is in scope, and the retry policy and the attempt component agree". But step 5's own taxonomy has at least three components varying per run — line 165 `<scope: tier and build tag>/<run: test name, seed, attempt>/`, and line 168 "**Run** makes one run distinct — it needs the attempt component". The noise components vary run-to-run too (line 170: "host name, scheduler job id, user name, a timestamp to the second"). Three consequences: (a) a correct name such as <tier-build>/<test>/<seed>/<attempt> fails the check; (b) a reader who obeys it literally converges on a single per-run component, which is exactly line 157's collision case — "Test name alone collides across seeds; seed alone across tests"; (c) the bullet self-contradicts, demanding one varying component and an attempt component in the same breath. The same singular error is at source in the slot table, line 48: "and which component of it varies per run". Fix both: the check should be that every component varying per run is labelled `run`, that together they make one run distinct (test name, seed and attempt at minimum), and that no `run` component is missing — not that there is exactly one.

MINOR — step 6 is titled "the four settings that manufacture fake failures" and enumerates resources / pass rule / copy-back / environment, none of which is retry; yet `retry : <the policy, and the directory a retry writes into>` is a block field and step 6 is its only plausible source (it Greps for "the strings the **Job resource and retry** slot names"). The slot is spent and C001 passes, but the step's own enumeration never tells the reader to write the field. Either add a fifth bullet or say in step 6 that the retry half of that slot is copied straight through and its directory comes from step 5's attempt component.

MINOR — line 228 overstates merge idempotence: "Merging one database twice adds not a single bin, so a duplicate is harmless *there*". True at the default at_least of 1, but mainstream merges accumulate per-bin hit counts, so where a bin's at_least is greater than 1 a double-merged database can push a below-threshold bin over and genuinely raise the number. The bullet's actionable advice ("Look in the counts, not the number") is right; it needs a half-clause hedge on the at_least case rather than a rewrite.
